newsitem.title: POLAND: LOT to set up charter flight firm in 1998.
newsitem.headline: LOT to set up charter flight firm in 1998.

text.p: Polish national airline PLL LOT SA will create a separate charter flight company next year to cater to the rapid growth in the charter flight business in Poland, a LOT official said on Thursday.
Adam Wychowaniec, head of LOT's charter flight department told a news confernce the number of such flights grew 50 percent in the first five months of this year against the same period last year.
"There are plans of setting up a LOT sister company which would deal only with charter flights. The process of creating such a company will take about a year," Wychowaniec said.
"In the first five months of this year we had 172 charter flights carrying 30,000 people and the peak will be in summer months with 10 flights a day," he said.

He said revenue from charter flights this year was expected to top 100 million zlotys against 47.5 million in 1996. The frequented routes were from Poland's major cities to Greece, Tunisia, Spain, Turkey, Egypt and Cyprus.
Bogdan Papis, the head of LOT's technical department, also present, said the company would start using two new Boeing 737-300 planes for charter flights in July.
"They have 145 seats and are specially built for tourist use without a division into business and economy class," Papis said.
